$comment: Text pool for the Addictive Behavior prayer category.
requests: Ninety days sober today. Thank you, Jesus, and thank you, church.
Strength for my brother, who is fighting addiction again.
My husband is starting a recovery program this week. It took a lot of courage for him to say yes. Pray for him to stick with it and for our family as we heal together.
I have been in recovery for two years, and lately the old pull has been strong. Pray for strength, for my sponsor, and for me to keep making the next right choice.
Our son is struggling with addiction and does not want help right now. We love him so much. Pray that he would come to the end of himself and turn to God.
A friend from work just told me he has a drinking problem and wants to quit. I am proud of him. Pray for courage as he starts this hard road.
My dad has been sober for one year! Pray for him to keep going strong, and thank God with us for this milestone.
Asking for prayer for my sister, who just went into a treatment program. She has tried before. Pray this time is different and that she finds real freedom.
Gambling has cost our family a lot. My husband is in a support group now and being honest with me. Pray for trust to be rebuilt and for him to stay free.
I just started attending a recovery group. It is hard to walk in each week, but the people there understand. Pray I keep showing up.

My wife has struggled with drinking for years. She hid it well, and I did not see how bad it was until recently. Last month she asked for help on her own, and she is now in an outpatient program. I am proud of her, and I am also hurt and tired. Pray for her recovery, for our marriage, and for our kids, who know more than we thought they did.

Today marks five years of sobriety for me. I still remember the night I walked into my first meeting, sure that nothing would change. God met me there, and He has been faithful every single day since. I am sharing this as a praise, but I also want prayer for the people in my group who are just starting out. Pray they would see that freedom is possible.
details: Recovery is one day at a time, and every day counts.
Pray for honest conversations and for trust to grow again.
The family needs prayer too, as everyone heals in their own way.
We know this is a long road, but God has not let go.
Good people and healthy friendships along the way would make a big difference.
Shame has been heavy, so pray for a deep sense of God's grace.
answers: Thank you for praying. Things are better than they were, one day at a time.
There have been some hard days, but we are moving forward with hope.
Answered prayer. More freedom than we have seen in years.
Not there yet, but there is real progress. We feel your prayers.
We are still waiting and praying, but we have peace that God is at work.
